name: Posteromedial approach to the distal tibia
corridor: Fragment-directed interval among tibia, posterior tibial tendon, FDL, and FHL with direct protection of posterior tibial neurovascular bundle

positioning.text: Position prone or in a stable lateral/supine variant that permits direct posteromedial access and planned fluoroscopic views.

setup.text: Use CT to select the safest tendon interval for the dominant fragment and plan neurovascular-bundle handling, posterior plate position, and any second incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark posteromedial tibial border, Achilles tendon, medial malleolus, posterior tibial tendon path, and posterior tibial pulse.

incision.text: Center incision at ankle between Achilles and posteromedial tibial border, continue proximally parallel to tibia and distally along posterior-tibial-tendon course.

superficial_interval.text: Open subcutaneous tissue and fascia to identify the deep fascial layer over posterior tibial tendon, FDL, neurovascular bundle, and FHL.

deep_interval.text: Select interval between tibia and posterior tibial tendon, between posterior tibial tendon and FDL, or between FDL and FHL; the last requires full direct bundle exposure and protection.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous fascia, flexor retinacular/deep fascia, selected tendon interval, posterior tibial periosteum, then posteromedial plafond.

structures_encountered.text: Posterior tibial tendon, FDL, FHL, posterior tibial artery/veins and tibial nerve, posterior capsule, and posteromedial tibia are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Posterior tibial neurovascular bundle, posterior tibial tendon blood supply, FDL/FHL, saphenous structures with medial extension, fragment blood supply, and cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Do not strip distal posterior tibial tendon from tibia; expose and control the neurovascular bundle directly before using the FDL-FHL interval.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the bundle only under direct view with broad protection and avoid focal pressure or traction on posterior tibial tendon and tibial nerve.

exposure.text: Provides direct reduction and posterior buttress access to posterior and medial fragments and can support medial-malleolar fixation through a full-thickness anteromedial flap.

limitations.text: The interval is anatomy-dense, far posterolateral and anterior fragments may be inaccessible, and tendon/bundle mobilization limits extension.

extensions.text: Create a full-thickness anteromedial flap for medial malleolus or add a separate posterolateral/anterior window for fragments outside the selected corridor.

indications.text: Use for posteromedial pilon, posterior-malleolar, and medial-fragment patterns requiring direct posterior buttress fixation.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose posterolateral or anterior exposure when dominant fragments lie outside the posteromedial corridor or the medial soft-tissue envelope is unsafe.

implant_implications.text: Supports direct posterior buttress plate placement; select an interval and plate position that avoid posterior tibial tendon and neurovascular impingement.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Preconfigure AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views for the chosen position and verify posterior reduction, plate location, and screw containment.

closure.text: Confirm bundle perfusion and hemostasis, restore each tendon to a free-gliding bed, repair fascia without constriction, and close full-thickness skin tension free.

complications.text: Complications include tibial neuropathy, posterior tibial vascular injury, tendon adhesions or irritation, wound breakdown, infection, malreduction, nonunion, and arthritis.

bailouts.text: Change to a safer adjacent tendon interval or add a second incision when direct bundle mobilization would be excessive or the fragment cannot be controlled.

procedure_applications.condition: Posteromedial and posterior plafond fragments require direct reduction and buttress fixation
A posteromedial posterior-malleolus fragment requires direct access

questions.question: What are the three deep intervals?
questions.answer: Tibia-posterior tibial tendon, posterior tibial tendon-FDL, or FDL-FHL.

questions.question: Which interval mandates direct bundle exposure?
What fixation principle does this approach enable?
questions.answer: Direct posterior buttress plating of posterior fragments.
